facts.condition: When the three auxiliaries have finite state sets, the repaired block objective is bounded and superadditive; consequently, its asymptotic per-use level is the supremum of its finite-block per-use levels.

Under Assumption A, a construction for an n-fold product channel can be serialized over the original memoryless BSSC while preserving its error behavior, making the block score divided by n an achievable sum-rate lower bound.
The randomized scheduling baseline has an exact algebraic optimizer and value, together with rigorous directed enclosures rather than an uncertified decimal approximation.

Under Assumptions A and B, the one-use finite-state Marton optimum equals the scheduling baseline; an n-use candidate improves that lower bound exactly when its block score is greater than n times the baseline.

assumptions: Assumption A: The classical Marton coding result applies to finite-state auxiliaries for finite two-receiver memoryless broadcast channels with average error.
Assumption B: For binary-input broadcast channels, optimizing the one-use Marton sum expression gives the same optimum as randomized receiver scheduling.
The scope excludes non-finite auxiliary spaces, and equality at a fixed blocklength is not assumed to provide a capacity converse.
